adjEbitda.title: Adjusted EBITDA
adjEbitda.content:
Adjusted EBITDA is Targa's own non-GAAP measure -- EBITDA before items like non-cash commodity hedge gains/losses and equity-method adjustments. It is what management guides to and the Street models.

For Targa: this is not the same number as the CSV's GAAP EBITDA column (see the Growth & Profitability section) -- the gap is mark-to-market hedge noise on NGL/gas forward positions, not cash earnings.

What to watch:

  • Growth versus the volume charts below -- is it price (commodity tailwind) or throughput (new capacity) doing the work?
  • Guidance beats/misses each quarter, since this is the metric the company itself targets

segmentAdjOperatingIncome.title: Adjusted operating income by segment
segmentAdjOperatingIncome.content:
Targa reports two segments: Gathering & Processing (G&P), which collects and processes wellhead gas (mostly Permian) into NGLs and residue gas, and Logistics & Transportation (L&T), which fractionates, stores, transports and exports the resulting NGLs and crude. Each dollar figure is the segment's own adjusted operating margin, not a percentage.

For Targa: L&T has historically carried the steadier, more fee-based margin while G&P is the more commodity- and volume-sensitive segment -- this chart is the split the consolidated AdjEBITDA line hides.

What to watch:

  • G&P margin tracking NGL/gas prices and Permian activity
  • L&T growing in step with the export and fractionation volumes below, since it is the less commodity-sensitive engine

gpGasVolumes.title: Gathering & Processing gas throughput
gpGasVolumes.content:
Plant inlet is raw wellhead gas entering Targa's processing plants (total and the Permian subset, which is the growth driver); natural gas sales is the residue gas sold after NGLs are stripped out.

For Targa: the Permian basin is the capacity-expansion story -- new plants (e.g. Pembrook, Bull Moose) are built to keep inlet volumes ahead of Permian producer activity.

What to watch:

  • Permian inlet growing faster than total inlet (basin concentration)
  • Inlet volumes outrunning announced plant capacity (bottleneck risk)

gpLiquidsVolumes.title: Gathering & Processing liquids volumes
gpLiquidsVolumes.content:
NGL production is the natural gas liquids stripped out at G&P plants (total and Permian); crude gathered is oil volumes collected on the same gathering systems; NGL sales is the segment's own marketed NGL volume.

For Targa: NGL production is the feedstock for the L&T segment's fractionation and export volumes below -- a gap opening up between the two signals third-party NGLs filling Targa's downstream capacity, or G&P volumes outrunning it.

What to watch:

  • NGL production growth versus fractionation growth (feedstock-to-downstream match)
  • Crude gathered, a smaller but higher-margin complement to the NGL business

ltVolumes.title: Logistics & Transportation volumes
ltVolumes.content:
Fractionation splits mixed NGLs into purity products (ethane, propane, butane, etc.) at Mont Belvieu; NGL pipeline transport moves NGLs from the Permian/other basins to the Gulf Coast; LPG exports is propane/butane shipped from Targa's own export terminal; NGL sales is the segment's marketed volume.

For Targa: this is the fee-based, lower-commodity-risk half of the business -- export capacity (expanded via the Gulf Coast Express-adjacent projects) is the bottleneck that sets how much of G&P's growing NGL production can reach international markets.

What to watch:

  • LPG exports relative to announced terminal capacity
  • Fractionation keeping pace with G&P NGL production (see the chart above)

realizedPrices.title: Realized commodity prices
realizedPrices.content:
The average price per unit Targa actually realized on uncontracted volumes: NGL ($/gal, blended purity-product basket), natural gas ($/MMBtu, can go negative in basis-constrained Permian conditions) and condensate ($/Bbl, priced off crude).

For Targa: most G&P contracts are percent-of-liquids or fee-based with a commodity-sensitive component, so these three prices -- not Targa's own volumes -- are usually the biggest single driver of G&P margin swings quarter to quarter.

What to watch:

  • Negative or near-zero realized natural gas price (Permian basis blowouts hurt G&P economics even as oil-directed drilling keeps NGL volumes growing)
  • NGL price direction versus the AdjEBITDA chart above

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Targa Resources Corp.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Targa Resources Corp.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Targa Resources Corp.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Targa Resources Corp.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Targa Resources Corp.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
